items.stem: Two states i and j communicate when:
items.explanation: Communication requires mutual reachability.

items.stem: A communicating class C is closed if:
options: No transition from C leads outside C
items.explanation: Closure means no positive-probability transition leaves the class.

items.stem: In a finite Markov chain, a closed communicating class is:
items.explanation: Every finite closed communicating class is recurrent.

items.stem: The period of state i is:
options: The gcd of all possible positive return times
items.explanation: The period is the gcd of n≥1 for which pᵢᵢ⁽ⁿ⁾>0.

items.stem: An absorbing state has period:
items.explanation: An absorbing state returns to itself at every positive time.

items.stem: A state can return at times 4, 6 and 10, and at no other positive times. Find its period.
items.check: The greatest common divisor of the possible return times is 2.

items.stem: For P=[[0,1,0],[1/2,0,1/2],[0,0,1]], which set is the closed communicating class?
items.explanation: States 1 and 2 communicate but state 2 can leave for 3; state 3 is absorbing.

items.stem: In the same chain P=[[0,1,0],[1/2,0,1/2],[0,0,1]], which states are transient?
items.explanation: The only closed class is {3}; in a finite chain states outside closed classes are transient.

items.stem: A state has possible return times {3,6,9,12,…}. Find its period.
items.explanation: The gcd of all positive return times is 3.
items.check: Every possible return time is a multiple of 3, and 3 itself is possible.

items.stem: For P=[[0,1],[1,0]], the period of each state is:
items.explanation: Returns occur at even positive times, whose gcd is 2.

items.stem: Which statements about communicating classes are true?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; a one-way edge alone does not create communication.
statements: Communicating classes partition the state space.
A closed class has no outgoing transition to its complement.
A one-way path from i to j implies i and j communicate.

A.why: Reachability is required in both directions.

C.why: This is the definition of a closed class.

D.why: The reverse path is also required.

items.stem: If a finite chain has two disjoint closed communicating classes, how many recurrent classes does it have?
items.explanation: Each finite closed communicating class is recurrent.

items.stem: A state can return at times 8, 12 and 20. Find its period.
items.check: All return times listed are divisible by 4, and gcd is 4.

items.stem: Which statement about states in the same communicating class is always true?
options: They have the same transition probabilities
They have the same stationary mass
items.explanation: Communicating states share their period.

items.stem: A finite chain has a unique closed communicating class C. Every state outside C is:
items.explanation: In a finite chain, states outside the closed classes are transient.

items.stem: A state has possible positive return times {6,10,14,18,…}. Find its period.
For a finite chain, which conclusion follows if a state belongs to a closed communicating class?
items.explanation: Finite closed communicating classes are recurrent.

items.stem: A state has possible return times including 3 and 5. What is its period?
items.explanation: The period is the gcd of all possible positive return times. Since 3 and 5 are both possible, the gcd of the full return-time set divides gcd(3,5)=1, so the period is 1.

items.stem: Which statements correctly describe recurrence and periodicity in a finite chain?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true; recurrence does not require aperiodicity.
statements: A closed communicating class is recurrent.
An absorbing state has period one.
A recurrent class can be periodic.
Every recurrent state must be aperiodic.

A.why: This is the finite-state classification theorem.

B.why: The absorbing state returns at all positive times.

C.why: The alternating two-state class is recurrent and period two.
